standard_prerequisites: The canonical map M \otimes_R R^N -> M^N (evaluate a finite tensor sum coordinatewise); Algebra, proposition-fg-tensor: for finitely generated M the map is surjective and its proof extracts generators from one tensor element
Countable modules: elements can be enumerated m_1, m_2, m_3, ...
core_obligations: If M is finite, the map is surjective by Algebra, proposition-fg-tensor
Conversely, assume the map surjective; enumerate M = m_1, m_2, m_3, ... and take a tensor element sum x_j \otimes a_j mapping to the sequence (m_n)
Then x_1, ..., x_m generate M over R: the same extraction of generators from a single preimage as in the proof of Algebra, proposition-fg-tensor, applied coordinatewise to the fixed tuple
proof_roadmap: Forward direction by the Algebra fg-tensor proposition
Under surjectivity, pick a preimage of the enumerated sequence (m_n)
Extract the finite generating set x_1, ..., x_m exactly as in the cited proof
